evidence (pooled): moderate: n=1 (a UKERC bucket row), no numbers at all. Base BOF electricity 0.09 GJ/t (n10). strong: electricity 0.094 (n1); capex and opex estimated.
why it might stay separate: Buckets are deliberate CIMS improvement steps.
reason: The moderate measures (fan drives, gas cleaning) act on a step that uses about 0.09 GJ/t of electricity, so even a 15% saving is about 0.01 GJ/t. With no data and nothing to save, the moderate step adds nothing. Set its single example to (none), or fold it into strong.

Compare same-source pairs (FMP BREF, NRCan 2007). If the saving stays under 15%, move the measures to efficiency-moderate; otherwise fix the base. Same family of issue as D02 and D04 in the earlier review.

Leave melting-furnace_isothermal apart (1.28, n1, about 26-31% lower), though one installation is weak evidence. Cross-family (other-industry). evidence (pooled): coupled-pickling: estimated, n=0, no numbers. Cold mill electricity 0.47 GJ/t (n3), fuel 0.81 (n3).
why it might stay separate: Coupling also absorbs the separate pickling line, which sits on the same node.
reason: Joining the lines saves handling and re-threading, a few per cent of the step's energy, which is a bucket-sized measure on the cold mill and not an option in its own right under design s2. Low priority because there are no data.

evidence (pooled): fuel 0.92 GJ/t (n2, 0.40-0.92, Barthe only) vs 0.99 (n3, 0.8-1.2): 7% apart. Visbreaking electricity 0.036-0.054 vs coking 0.096. No capex for either

evidence (pooled): solid-sorbent: 1 example (Plaza 2020 RTI sorbent, Brevik), no pooled values. amine: capex 467 (n53), heat 3.42 GJ/t (n9)

Also, capture-unit_amine's examples-named still lists 'Solid sorbent capture; Calcium looping', which is stale. Calcium looping was re-added with numbers and burns its own fuel (different emissions), so I'm not proposing to fold that back.

reason: Both abate centrifugal-compressor wet-seal methane, in the same unit and on the same node. Wet-seal has no cost data, so as its own archetype it gives CIMS nothing. Merge, and let the cost range show the two approaches. Keep it separate only if a source prices it.

proposal: combustion-turbine_simple-cycle (label 'Engine or simple-cycle turbine generator, power only')
evidence (pooled): efficiency 33.3% (n1) vs 35.1% (n2; electricity 28.7% n14). capex 21.8 (n1) vs 43.6 (n15). Both emit combustion CO2. simple-cycle already holds landfill-gas engines and a light-fuel-oil turbine (DEA).
why it might stay separate: The diesel set is the off-grid incumbent where gas is unavailable, and CIMS may need it as a fuel-availability option. A cleaner split would be by equipment, engine vs turbine, rather than by carrier. Capex differs 2x, from a single source.
reason: Under §2 a carrier difference alone is not an archetype; energy is within 6% and the emissions are of the same kind. The current split is by carrier, yet gas engines already sit with turbines.
